question: How many 5-digit numbers have at least one zero?
solution:
Count all five-digit numbers and subtract those with no zero. The first digit has $9$ choices ($1$ through $9$), and each of the other four digits has $10$ choices, giving $9\cdot10^4=90{,}000$ numbers. If zero is forbidden, each of the five digits has $9$ choices, giving $9^5=59{,}049$ numbers. Thus $90{,}000-59{,}049=30{,}951$ have at least one zero.
Final answer: 30,951
